haiku-low.q1: Keys load at startup before readiness. Readiness becomes true only after all three secrets are loaded and their version ids recorded; /healthz returns 200 only then.
haiku-low.q2: It retries (4 attempts, about 6 seconds), then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes it re-reads all three. If all succeed, it swaps in the new values and logs version ids. If any read fails, it keeps all last good values, logs a warning, and stays ready.
haiku-low.q4: Only in the in-memory holder object. Key values must never appear in environment variables, files, temp files, log lines, or request-logging middleware.
haiku-low.q5: The orders-api-prod pod identity reads orders-api/prod/*. Security on-call writes it. Engineers have no read access to prod paths.
haiku-low.q6: Old keys remain in git history and past images, so they count as leaked. They become harmless only when replaced and revoked at each provider, after usage checks confirm no consumer uses them.
haiku-low.q7: Clients stop copying the key in constructors. Each call reads the current key from the holder, so a refreshed value is used on the next call without restart.
haiku-low.q8: Wait one 5-minute refresh cycle plus a margin. Confirm every pod's latest logged version id is new, and confirm provider usage reports show zero old-key usage for the whole window.
haiku-low.q9: Store access (step 2), then app code merged (step 9), then rotate at providers and write new keys to the store (step 10), then remove keys from config (step 17), then roll out (step 12).
haiku-low.q10: make run loads the dev secret path using the developer's dev-only identity. It never reads prod, and local config holds no keys. Engineers delete old local live-key copies.
haiku-low.q11: After retries, it logs the error and exits non-zero. The pod never becomes ready, so the rollout halts.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first; readiness (/healthz 200) is true only after all three secrets are loaded.
sonnet.q2: It retries, then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected (maxUnavailable: 0).
sonnet.q3: A background refresh re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes and swaps them into the holder if all reads succeed. If any read fails, it keeps the last good values for all three, logs a warning, and stays ready.
sonnet.q4: Held in process memory (the holder) only. Never in environment variables, files/disk cache/temp files, log lines, or request-logging middleware.
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod pod identity (plus KMS decrypt on prod key). Write: security on-call. Engineers cannot read prod paths; developer identity reads dev only.
sonnet.q6: Git history is not rewritten, so the old keys remain in past commits and count as leaked. They become harmless by being replaced with new keys at each provider and the old keys revoked at the provider.
sonnet.q7: Provider clients no longer copy the key in constructors; each call reads the current key from the holder, so a refresh takes effect without restart.
sonnet.q8: Step 13: wait at least one refresh cycle (5 min) plus margin, then confirm every pod's latest logged version id is the new one and old-key usage at that provider has been zero for the whole window (per-provider usage reports).
sonnet.q9: Order: create store access (step 2), dev keys (3), code to read from store (4-8), merge without promoting (9), rotate and write new keys to the store (10), verify prod read (11), remove keys from config plus CI guard (17/16, merged after 9, before rollout), rolling deploy (12), confirm (13), block rollback (15), revoke old keys (14). Keys are rotated at providers (creating new ones) before copying into the store; old keys revoked last.
sonnet.q10: From the dev secret path orders-api/dev/*, using the developer's dev-only identity (non-production/sandbox keys); never the prod path or live keys.
sonnet.q11: After retries, if any secret is still missing, it logs the error and exits non-zero; the pod never becomes ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Rotation cadence is an undecided open question; the plan sets none.
